faq.title: Frequently Asked Questions
faq.sub: Everything you need to know before booking.

items.q: How often should I service my HVAC system?
items.a: We recommend a tune-up twice a year — once before heating season and once before cooling season. Regular maintenance extends equipment life and keeps your warranty valid.

items.q: What's the difference between R-410A and R-32 refrigerant?
items.a: R-32 is the newer, more eco-friendly refrigerant with a lower global warming potential. New systems use R-32; if you have an older R-410A system we'll walk you through your options.

items.q: When should I repair vs. replace my system?
items.a: If the repair cost exceeds 50% of a new system's cost, or your equipment is over 15 years old, replacement usually makes more financial sense. We'll give you an honest recommendation either way.

items.q: How can I improve my home's energy efficiency?
items.a: Regular filter changes (every 1–3 months), sealing duct leaks, adding a programmable thermostat, and annual tune-ups are the highest-impact steps. We offer a free energy audit with any service call.

The work splits two ways. Some days it is a no cool call where a homeowner needs the air back on. Other days it is a planned job, a furnace replaced, a heat pump put in, ducts cleaned and sealed. We handle both, and we tell you which one you are actually looking at before anything gets ordered.

We hold Class A Certification, NATE Certification and EPA 608 Certification, and we are BBB Accredited and an Energy Star Partner. We are licensed and insured. We service and install a wide range of equipment, including Trane, Carrier, Lennox, Rheem, Daikin, Goodman, Bosch, York, Mitsubishi Electric and more, so you are not pushed toward one label.

Homeowners make up most of our work, and we also look after property managers who need several units kept running on one schedule. Office hours are 8am to 5pm, our typical response time is 2 hours, and new customers get $50 off their first service. Call (207) 569-3204 or email hello@bridgertonheatingcooling.com.

page.intro: Bridgerton Heating & Cooling repairs and replaces furnaces for homeowners and property managers in Orlando. Call (207) 569-3204 between 8am and 5pm and we will book a service call. Estimates on a new furnace are free.
body: If your furnace has stopped heating, a technician needs to see it running before anyone can say what is wrong. We come out, test the unit, and tell you what we found and what it will cost before any work starts. Some faults are a part swap. Others mean the furnace is near the end of its life, and we will say so.

Age, repair history and safety all play into the repair or replace call. A cracked heat exchanger or a failed control board on an older unit usually points to replacement. A dirty flame sensor, a worn blower motor or a clogged filter usually does not.

When a new furnace is the right answer, we pull the old one out, set the new one in place, and test it before we leave. We work on all brands, including Trane, American Standard, Carrier, Bryant, Payne, Lennox, Rheem, Armstrong Air, Mitsubishi Electric, Fujitsu, LG and Tempstar.
includedNotes: We test for carbon monoxide so you know the furnace is burning safely and nothing is leaking into the house.
We service and repair every brand we come across, so you are not stuck because of the badge on the cabinet.
We replace a blower motor that has seized, is noisy, or is no longer pushing air through the ducts.
A fresh filter goes in, which protects the blower and keeps airflow where it should be.
On a replacement we haul the old furnace away, so there is nothing left in the basement or closet for you to deal with.
signNotes: Usually a thermostat, power, or ignition fault. Check the breaker and the thermostat batteries first, then call us to diagnose it.
A light dusty smell on the first cold day is normal. A sharp electrical or plastic smell is not. Shut the furnace off and call us.
Squealing often points at the blower motor or belt, banging at delayed ignition, rattling at a loose panel. Any of them is worth a look before it gets worse.
Usually a dirty or failing thermocouple, or a draft in the flue. It needs testing rather than relighting over and over.
Could be fuel supply, ignition, a tripped safety switch, or a dead blower. We diagnose it on site and tell you what it will take.

page.intro: Bridgerton Heating & Cooling installs and services air conditioning for homes and rental properties in Orlando. Call (207) 569-3204 during business hours to get on the schedule. The estimate for a new system is free.
body: An AC that is not cooling is usually one of a few things. Low refrigerant from a leak, a dirty coil choking airflow, a failed capacitor, or a clogged drain line that has tripped the safety switch. We check the system, find the cause, and tell you what the fix is before we start.

Replacement is the better answer when the system is old, the repairs are stacking up, or the unit was never the right size for the house in the first place. An oversized unit short cycles and leaves the air damp. An undersized one runs all day and never catches up. We size the system to your home rather than matching whatever was there before.

On an install we remove the old unit, set and start the new one, test it, and handle the permit and inspection. We install Trane, American Standard, Carrier, Bryant, Payne, Lennox, Armstrong Air, Mitsubishi Electric, Fujitsu, LG, Tempstar and Amana.
includedNotes: The old unit comes out and goes with us.
We pull the permit and see the inspection through, so the work is on record and signed off.
We start the system, check pressures and airflow, and confirm it is cooling properly before we leave.
A new thermostat goes in with the system and we set it up with you.
We measure and size the system for your home so it cools evenly and runs the way it should.
signNotes: Often low refrigerant, a dirty coil, or a failed compressor or capacitor. It needs testing, so call us rather than letting it run.
Usually power, the thermostat, or a tripped float switch in the drain pan. Check the breaker, then call us.
Normally a blocked condensate drain line or a frozen coil. Shut the system off so the water stops and book a visit.
Grinding or screeching points at a motor bearing, buzzing at an electrical fault. Turn it off and have it looked at.
A system that is losing efficiency, often from a dirty coil, a refrigerant leak, or ductwork. Worth a service visit to find where the energy is going.
Around that age parts get harder to source and efficiency drops off. Ask us for a free estimate on a replacement and compare it against the repair.
